newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen falling after baht float.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen falling after baht float.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to drop and be quite volatile on Wednesday on investor jitters following Thailand's decision to float the baht effective immediately, brokers said.

"I think the stock market would be volatile today in line with the fall in the baht against the dollar this morning shortly after the central bank announced that the baht would be floated," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index closed down 0.90 points at 527.28 on 3.46 billion baht turnover on Monday. Tuesday was a holiday.
The Bank of Thailand and the Ministry of Finance announced earlier that the Thai exchange rate system would be a changed to a managed float, effective on Wednesday.
The authorities did not detail how the float would work, but said the value of the baht would be determined by market forces to reflect fundamental economic forces.
Previously the baht was set against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
Brokers said investors believed that non-performing loans of financial institutions would rise due to the effect of the float on dollar-denominated loans.--Suthep Chawla 662-652-0642
